subject: Clarify: default artifacts storage window for prompts vs outputs
messages:
From: Julie Nguyen <julie.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify default storage: prompts vs outputs and deletion flow

Hi Alex,

Quick question as we finalize our vendor security review: can you confirm Redwood's default retention windows for the following artifact categories when using the hosted API (no custom retention set by customer)?

- Full request/response payloads (raw prompts + model tokens)
- Prompts only (customer-provided prompt text)
- Model outputs (generated text returned to app)
- Operational telemetry (latency, error logs, token counts)

We also need to understand how deletions are handled: is there an immediate delete-by-id API for individual items? If a customer requests full purge, what are expected timelines and whether backups/replicas are removed within the same window? Finally, since we are US-based with EU customers, can you confirm data residency controls for logs (region pinning)?

Thanks — need to capture the answers in the RES-ACME vendor questionnaire.

Julie
Security Engineer
Acme Corp
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Nguyen <julie.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify default storage: prompts vs outputs and deletion flow

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by a few implementation notes and links.

Summary (defaults for hosted API):
- Full request/response payloads (complete logs that include prompt + model token stream): 14 days by default.
- Prompts only (customer-supplied prompt text indexed as input artifacts): 90 days by default.
- Model outputs (generated text returned to caller): 90 days by default.
- Operational telemetry (metrics, token counts, latencies): aggregated metrics are retained for 365 days; detailed per-request telemetry (trace-level) follows the 14-day policy.

Deletion and purge behavior:
- Customer-level immediate deletes: We provide a Delete Request API that can target a conversation or request-id — when invoked, the item is marked for deletion and removed from the primary store within 24–48 hours.
- Backups/replicas: Backups are encrypted and have a separate lifecycle; when a purge is requested, we schedule removal from hot stores immediately and from backup/replica windows within the next backup cycle (up to 30 days depending on region/DR settings).
- Certified attestation: For customers needing an auditable purge, we can provide an evidence packet (log of deletion job run + job ids).

Data residency controls:
- By default hosted API customers are routed to the nearest region. Customers can pick a home-region (us / eu / apac) in account settings; logs and artifacts are pinned to that region for storage and replication.
- EU-pin customers have all artifacts stored in eu-west1 with no cross-border replication unless explicitly enabled.

Notes and caveats:
- "Prompts only" retention applies when we can trivially extract and classify the prompt as a customer-provided input. If prompts are embedded in a more complex payload, the extraction process and classification may affect retention labeling.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments customers control retention windows via config and local policies — the above defaults are for hosted API only.

I attached a short table (SLA_Data_Retention_Table.xlsx) and a residency diagram that maps account setting -> storage buckets. If you'd like an explicit line for your questionnaire, I can prepare a one-paragraph answer that you can paste into the form.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Forwarding so we have the purge SLA details inline. Alex — two small clarifications we should add to the customer answer:

1) For the Delete Request API, please confirm whether deletion is eventual (tombstone + async GC) or synchronous removal from indexes. If eventual, we should state the expected window (24–48h) and that there may be up to 30 days for complete removal from cold backups.

2) Add an explicit statement about PI/PHI: we treat any content customers self-identify as PI as subject to the same process but with optional extended confirmation and evidence packet for compliance teams.

Rishi — can you confirm the backup/replica window wording?

-Marissa (on behalf of Alex)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Nguyen <julie.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify default storage: prompts vs outputs and deletion flow

Julie — quick follow-up with the tightened language Marissa suggested and explicit references for your questionnaire.

1) Default retention windows (hosted API):
- Full request/response payloads: 14 days (hot store).
- Prompts only (customer-supplied): 90 days.
- Model outputs: 90 days.
- Aggregated telemetry: 365 days. Detailed per-request telemetry: 14 days.

2) Deletion behavior and SLA:
- Delete Request API behavior: deletion is processed as follows: the object is tombstoned immediately and removed from active indexes within 24–48 hours. A background GC job clears tombstoned items from cold storage and backups within the next backup cycle (standard window up to 30 days). For customers requiring quicker removal from backups we offer a paid expedited purge that reduces the backup removal window to 7–10 days (requires signed request).

3) Backups and replicas: backups are encrypted at rest with KMS-managed keys. Backup retention/replication varies by region and DR class — default backup purge window is 30 days for hosted accounts in the US.

4) Data residency: customers can set an account-level home region. For eu-pin accounts, logs and artifacts are stored in eu-west1 with no cross-border replication unless customer enables multi-region DR.

5) PI/PHI handling: if you mark a dataset as PI/PHI in support, we escalate the purge to provide an attestation packet and can route deletion windows through an extended compliance workflow.

Attached: SLA_Data_Retention_Table.xlsx (simple table of artifact -> hot store TTL -> backup purge window), redwood-data-residency-diagram.png.

If this works, I'll send a single-paragraph answer for the vendor questionnaire and include the attestation option language.

Cheers,
Alex
